content: AI-generated statistical reports must: (1) cite only computed/provided values — LLMs fabricate financial metrics when not grounded; GPT-4-Turbo with retrieval incorrectly answered or refused 81% of SEC filing questions without explicit grounding; (2) use calibrated uncertainty language — hedging words like 'potentially', 'possibly', 'suggests' rather than definitive claims; models tend to prioritize decisiveness over expressing uncertainty, averaging 94% confidence regardless of explanation quality; (3) match scope of grounding — statements about trend must be grounded in trend data; (4) flag the joint hypothesis problem in event studies (abnormal return tests jointly test the event AND the model). Anti-patterns: fabricating p-values, overclaiming significance from borderline results, omitting confidence intervals, verbose boilerplate that restates inputs rather than interpreting them, ignoring the bad-model problem.
